title: Recruiting Software Pricing Guide for Hiring Teams
description: A detailed look at pricing models for applicant tracking systems, recruiting CRMs, and interview platforms, with cost comparisons across Lever, Greenhouse, BambooHR, Workday, and Zoho People.
body:
Recruiting software pricing encompasses a wide range of models, from per-employee subscriptions to per-job-posting fees to per-hire transaction costs. Understanding these pricing structures is essential for accurately budgeting talent acquisition technology.

This guide examines the pricing models used by the major recruiting platform categories and provides cost comparison guidance. None of the platforms evaluated have published pricing verification data, so check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Applicant Tracking System Pricing

Applicant tracking systems form the core of recruiting technology. ATS platforms manage job postings, resume collection, candidate communication, interview scheduling, and offer management.

The most common ATS pricing model is per-employee-per-month, typically ranging from a few dollars to over ten dollars per employee per month for full-featured platforms. This model means that organizations with larger headcounts pay more, even if their hiring volume is relatively low relative to company size.

Some ATS platforms use per-job-posting pricing, charging a monthly fee for each active job. This model can be more cost-effective for organizations with many employees but low turnover. Per-job pricing typically ranges from several tens to over a hundred dollars per active job per month.

Enterprise ATS platforms often use custom pricing based on employee count, hiring volume, and selected feature modules. These contracts frequently include implementation services and dedicated support.

Check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates, as ATS pricing is frequently customized.

## Recruiting CRM Pricing

Recruiting CRMs focus on candidate relationship management, sourcing, and pipeline building. These platforms help recruiting teams proactively engage passive candidates and maintain relationships with past applicants.

CRM pricing typically follows a per-user-per-month model, with costs scaling with the number of recruiting team members rather than total employee count. This model can be more cost-effective for organizations with large workforces but small recruiting teams.

CRM platforms may also charge based on candidate database size or the number of active sourcing campaigns. Integration with job boards and social media platforms sometimes incurs additional costs.

Check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates, as CRM pricing varies based on team size and feature requirements.

## Interview Scheduling and Assessment Tools

Interview scheduling tools automate the logistics of coordinating candidates, interviewers, and room availability. Assessment platforms provide skills testing and evaluation tools.

These tools are often priced per-interview or per-assessment, making them variable costs that scale with hiring volume. Per-interview pricing for scheduling tools typically ranges from a modest fee to a few dollars per scheduled interview. Technical assessment platforms charge per assessment with volume discounts available.

The total cost of interview tools should account for both scheduled interviews and no-shows or cancellations, as some platforms charge for all scheduled assessments regardless of completion.

Check each vendor's current pricing page for exact rates.

## Cost Drivers and Inflection Points

Several factors drive recruiting software costs beyond base subscription pricing:

Job board integration fees add to total cost. Many ATS platforms charge extra for direct posting to major job boards, and job boards themselves charge per posting or subscription fees that compound with recruiting platform costs.

AI-powered screening and matching features typically require premium plan tiers. Platforms that offer automated resume screening, candidate ranking, and skills matching reserve these capabilities for higher-priced plans.

Video interviewing integration is another cost driver. While many ATS platforms include basic video interview capabilities, advanced features like recorded interviews, asynchronous screening, and AI-powered interview analysis require premium plans.

Implementation and configuration costs are significant for enterprise ATS deployments. Custom workflow configuration, integration with existing HR systems, and team training typically add twenty to thirty percent to first-year costs.

## Budget Planning Recommendations

When budgeting for recruiting software, project total cost based on current hiring volume with a growth buffer. Multi-year agreements often provide per-interview or per-hire pricing discounts but require accurate volume forecasting.

Evaluate feature tiers carefully. Some mid-tier ATS plans provide sufficient capabilities for organizations with straightforward hiring processes, while organizations with high-volume or specialized hiring needs may require enterprise-level features.

Consider total cost of ownership across the recruiting technology stack rather than individual tool pricing. Integrated platforms that combine ATS, CRM, and assessment capabilities may offer cost advantages over separately purchased best-of-breed tools.
